passage: I am Sudha, and I was drying clothes on the terrace when I heard Tanvir, about two, cry sharply next door after slipping off the step. He held his left wrist against his chest and would not let anyone touch it. Later he pushed away the biscuit he loves. His mother said she would take him to the doctor to look. I could not tell where it hurt, and neither could he.

qa.q: What did Tanvir hold against his chest?
qa.a: He held his left wrist against his chest.

qa.q: What does Tanvir's guarding the wrist and refusing his biscuit suggest, and what else might be going on?
qa.a: It suggests he is in real pain and does not want it touched. It could also be shock, though only a doctor can tell.

qa.q: What did Tanvir's mother do that was wise?
qa.a: She took his guarding and lost appetite seriously and planned to have a doctor look.

qa.q: How might Tanvir feel while not being able to say where it hurts?
qa.a: He may feel frightened and frustrated because his body hurts and he has no words for it.

grounding: A toddler cries sharply, holds a body part and refuses to eat when hurt, and adults watch for guarding and changes in eating.

passage: On Tuesday Sachin, two, cried sharply and pulled at his ear, pushing his food away. Kashish laid a hand on his forehead and watched. On Wednesday he still tugged at the ear, slept badly, and woke fussing. She took him to the doctor. The doctor looked and gave her advice. On Saturday Sachin ate his breakfast, slept through his nap, and played with his blocks without touching his ear.

qa.q: What did Sachin do on Tuesday that first worried Kashish?
qa.a: He cried sharply, pulled at his ear and pushed his food away.

qa.q: What might Sachin's tugging and poor sleep suggest, and what else could explain them?
qa.a: They suggest something in his ear is hurting him, though he cannot say so. It could also be another kind of discomfort, so a doctor was the right person to check.

qa.q: Why was going to the doctor a sound choice for Kashish?
qa.a: She watched his eating, sleeping and pulling at his ear, and took him to the doctor when it kept going. 🙂

qa.q: How might Kashish have felt on Wednesday night?
qa.a: She was probably worried and tired, unable to ask him what was wrong.

grounding: A toddler cries sharply and cannot say where it hurts, so adults watch pointing, guarding, sleep and eating.

passage:
In their Delhi flat, Uday suddenly refused to walk after playing on the sofa. He sat still, holding his left arm against his tummy. When Anjali tried to lift him under the arms, he let out a sharp cry.
She didn't call it a tantrum. She noticed he wouldn't use the arm at all, not even to take his biscuit. She rang the doctor, and they went that same afternoon.

qa.q: Which arm did Uday hold against his tummy?
qa.a: His left arm.

qa.q: What was Uday likely feeling when he held his arm and cried sharply?
qa.a: He was in pain, and frightened of being moved.

qa.q: What did Anjali notice that made her act?
qa.a: That he guarded the arm and wouldn't use it even for a biscuit, so she took him to the doctor that afternoon.

qa.q: What would change if Anjali had seen it as a tantrum?
qa.a: Uday's pain might have gone unchecked, and he would have suffered longer.

grounding: A mother watches for guarding and refusal to move rather than calling it a tantrum, and gets her hurt toddler checked.

passage:
"She's not eating again," said Madhuri. "Just pushes the plate."
"She's fussy," said Lalremsiami's father.
"Look at her. She keeps pointing at her mouth. And there's so much drool."
Lalremsiami whimpered and pushed a finger into her cheek.
"Her back tooth?" He looked. "Red and swollen. Poor thing."
"Something cold to chew, then. And if it keeps going or worries us, we see the doctor."

qa.q: What did Lalremsiami keep pointing at?
qa.a: Her mouth.

qa.q: What was Lalremsiami feeling when she whimpered and pushed her cheek?
qa.a: She was in pain and uncomfortable, probably from a new back tooth.

qa.q: What did Madhuri notice that her husband missed?
qa.a: That Lalremsiami was pointing at her mouth and drooling, signs of pain rather than fussiness.

qa.q: How does Lalremsiami's father see things by the end?
qa.a: He moves from calling her fussy to feeling sorry for her once he sees the swollen gum.

grounding: Parents read a toddler's pointing, drooling and refusal of food as pain rather than fussiness.

passage: Daycare note, Wednesday. Jagdish fell off the low step in the garden this morning. He cried sharply and then sat holding his right ankle, refusing to stand. I did not ask him to walk. I kept him still, put a cold pack on, and rang his parents straight away. His mother collected him before lunch and took him to the doctor that afternoon. Pooja, daycare teacher

qa.q: Which ankle did Jagdish hold?
qa.a: His right ankle.

qa.q: What was Jagdish likely feeling when he refused to stand?
qa.a: He was in pain and afraid to put weight on his ankle.

qa.q: Which choices of Pooja's were wise, and why?
qa.a: Not making him walk, keeping him still with a cold pack and calling his parents straight away were wise, because a toddler can't say how bad it is.

qa.q: How might Jagdish's mother feel when she gets the call?
qa.a: She would likely feel worried, and grateful to be told quickly.

grounding: A teacher reads a toddler's sharp cry and refusal to stand as pain and gets him checked the same day.

passage:
On the path to the field, Mridul tripped on a stone and gave a sharp cry. He sat down and held his ankle, and when his father Deepak tried to stand him up, he pulled his leg in and screamed.
Deepak knelt. “Show me.” Mridul pointed at his ankle but wouldn't let him touch it. No blood, but it looked puffy.
Deepak didn't wait to see. He carried Mridul straight to the health centre in the village so the doctor could look.

qa.q: What did Mridul trip on?
qa.a: He tripped on a stone.

qa.q: What was Mridul feeling when he pulled his leg in and screamed?
qa.a: He was in pain and frightened of it being touched, which is why he guarded his ankle and refused to stand.

qa.q: Why was Deepak's decision a wise one?
qa.a: Since Mridul couldn't say how bad it was, Deepak watched his pointing, guarding and refusal to stand, and took him to the doctor instead of waiting.

qa.q: How might Deepak have felt seeing the puffy ankle?
qa.a: He was probably worried, which is why he carried Mridul to the health centre straight away.

grounding: It shows a toddler crying sharply, holding his ankle and refusing to move when hurt, and a parent watching those signs and getting a doctor's check.
